shared_context.topic: How to tell a canker sore from herpes/cold sore
shared_context.condition: Oral lesion differentiation between canker sores and herpes simplex cold sores

atoms.1: Canker sores and cold sores (caused by herpes simplex virus, HSV) are two distinct oral mucosal lesions with different causes and characteristics.
atoms.2: Canker sores typically appear as small, shallow ulcers with a yellow or white base and a red border.
atoms.3: Canker sores usually occur on the inside of the mouth, including the cheeks, lips, tongue, and gums.
atoms.4: Canker sores are often accompanied by pain, tenderness, and a burning sensation.
atoms.5: Canker sores can be triggered by stress, hormonal changes, food sensitivities, or minor mouth injuries.
atoms.6: Canker sores typically resolve on their own within 1-3 weeks without treatment.
atoms.7: Cold sores (caused by Herpes Simplex Virus, HSV) typically appear as small, fluid-filled blisters that eventually rupture and form a crust.
atoms.8: Cold sores usually occur on the lips.
atoms.9: Cold sores can also appear on the mouth, nose, or genital area.
atoms.10: Cold sores are often accompanied by tingling, itching, or burning sensations before the blisters appear.
atoms.11: Cold sores can be triggered by stress, sunlight, or other factors that weaken the immune system.
atoms.12: Cold sores may recur, especially if the virus is not treated or managed properly.
atoms.13: To determine whether a lesion is a canker sore or a cold sore, consider the location.
atoms.14: Canker sores typically occur inside the mouth.
atoms.15: Cold sores usually appear on the lips or other external areas.
atoms.16: To determine whether a lesion is a canker sore or a cold sore, consider the appearance.
atoms.17: Canker sores have a yellow or white base and a red border.
atoms.18: Cold sores are fluid-filled blisters that eventually form a crust.
atoms.19: To determine whether a lesion is a canker sore or a cold sore, consider the symptoms.
atoms.20: Canker sores are often accompanied by pain and tenderness.
atoms.21: Cold sores may be preceded by tingling or itching sensations.
atoms.22: If you are unsure about the nature of a lesion, consult a healthcare professional for proper evaluation and guidance.
atoms.23: If a lesion persists or worsens, consult a healthcare professional for proper evaluation and guidance.

snippets.output: Canker sores and cold sores (caused by herpes simplex virus, HSV) are two distinct oral mucosal lesions with different causes and characteristics.
If you are unsure about the nature of a lesion or if it persists or worsens, consult a healthcare professional for proper evaluation and guidance.

To determine whether an oral lesion is a canker sore or a herpes simplex cold sore, consider the location: canker sores typically occur inside the mouth, while herpes simplex cold sores usually appear on the lips or other external areas.

To determine whether an oral lesion is a canker sore or a herpes simplex cold sore, consider the appearance: canker sores have a yellow or white base with a red border, while herpes simplex cold sores are fluid-filled blisters that eventually form a crust.

To determine whether an oral lesion is a canker sore or a herpes simplex cold sore, consider the symptoms: canker sores are often accompanied by pain and tenderness, while herpes simplex cold sores may be preceded by tingling or itching sensations.

Canker sores typically appear as small, shallow ulcers with a yellow or white base and a red border, usually on the inside of the mouth including the cheeks, lips, tongue, and gums, and are often accompanied by pain, tenderness, and a burning sensation.
Canker sores can be triggered by stress, hormonal changes, food sensitivities, or minor mouth injuries, and canker sores typically resolve on their own within 1–3 weeks without treatment.

snippets.output: Cold sores caused by Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) typically appear as small, fluid-filled blisters that eventually rupture and form a crust, and they are often accompanied by tingling, itching, or burning sensations before the blisters appear. Cold sores usually occur on the lips but can also appear on the mouth, nose, or genital area.
Cold sores can be triggered by stress, sunlight, or other factors that weaken the immune system, and cold sores may recur, especially if the virus is not treated or managed properly.
